caseno: Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 33624 of 2010 with No. 9833 of 2008 and Criminal Appeal No. 1773 of 2002 and Jail Appeal No. 387 of 2002.
lawyer:
AY Ahmed Ali, Advocate—For the Accused-Petitioner. 
Sanwar Ahmed, Advocate—For the Accused-Appellant.
parties:
Mohor Ali & 3 ors ----- Petitioner
Vs
State ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Md. Moinul Islam Chowdhury J : At the instance of the convict-petitioner, Md. Mohor Ali alias Mohor, in the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 33624 of 2010, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 20-05-2002 passed in Nari-o-Shishu Case No. 17- of 2000 arising out of Kaligonj Police Station Case No. 09 dated 16-05-2000 corresponding to GR No- 189 of 200 by the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Satkhira convicting the petitioner under sections 5, 6 and 30 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Ain, 2000 and sentencing him to suffer imprisonment for life and also to pay a fine of Tk. 5,000 in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year more should not be quashed, and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. At the instance of convict-petitioner, Md. Nazrul Islam alias Nazrul Islam l3arkandaj, in the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 9833 of 2008, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 20-05-2002 passed in Nari-o-Shishu Case No. 177 of 2000 arising out of Kaligonj Police Station Case No. 09 dated 16-05-2000 corresponding to GR No. 189 of 2000 by the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Satkhira convicting the petitioner under sections 5, 6 and 30 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Ain, 2000 and sentencing him to suffer imprisonment for life and also to pay a fine of Tk. 5,000 in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year more should not be quashed, and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. At the instance of the convict-appellant, Ismail Sarder, the Criminal Appeal No. 1773 of 2002 was preferred impugning the judgment and order dated 20-05-2002 passed in Nari-o-Shishu Case No. 177 of 2000 arising out of Kaligonj Police Station Case No. 09 dated 16-05-2000 corresponding to GR No. 189 of 2000 by the learned Judge. Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Satkhira convicting the petitioner under sections 5, 6 and 30 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Ain, 2000 and sentencing him to suffer imprisonment for life and also to pay a fine of Tk. 5,000 in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year more. 

 4. At the instance of the convict, Yousuf Ali, this Jail Appeal No. 387 of 2002 was preferred impugning the judgment and order dated 20-05-2002 passed in Nari-o-Shishu Case No. 177 of 2000 arising out of Kaligonj Police Station Case No. 09 dated 16-05-2000 corresponding to GR No. 189 of 2000 by the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Satkhira convicting the petitioner under sections 5,6 and 30 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Ain, 2000 and sentencing him to suffer imprisonment for life and also to pay a fine of Tk. 5,000 in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year more. 

 5. As the aforesaid Miscellaneous Cases, the Criminal appeal and the Jail Appeal were filed by the different convict-appellants impugning the same judgment and order passed by the same court we are taking all of them together for disposal by a single judgment. 

 6. The relevant facts for disposal of these Miscellaneous Cases, the Criminal Appeal and the Jail Appeal as presented by the prosecution in short, are that the informant lodged a first information report against 8 accused persons including the accused-petitioners/appellants alleging inter alia that informant received a secret information that 8/9 young women and a child have been kept in the residence of Nazrul in order to traffic them to India. On the basis of the said information as per GD Entry No. 571 dated 16-05-2000 the informant along with his police personnel started for the residence of said Nazrul of said Nazrul at Village Gobindapur and on the way as to when they reached at Dhalbaria Junction at about 12-30 P.M. they recovered young women along with a child and caught hold 4(four) accused persons, namely, Abdul Mannan, Yousuf, Alam and Saiful Islam by the local people who are Md. Jabbar Ali, Shawkat Sheikh, Puti Sheikh and others. The informant and his companions and the local people took the victims and the accused to the Kaliganj Police Station and on interrogation the accused persons confessed as to the offence and disclosed the names of their associates namely, Ahmed Hossain, Ismail and Nazim Uddin who have fled away. On interrogation the recovered women informed that they were brought in the residence of accused Nazrul assuring them to provide in service in India. The recovered victims Jasmine, Fatema and Romesa were beaten as they refused to reside in the residence of Nazrul which caused injury on the left eye of the victim Jasmine. They further learned that the accused persons brought away another two victims namely Nazma and Jostna on 13-05-2000 from a slum situated at the back side of Tongi Medical and the said victims were also kept in the residence of accused Nazrul and they were managed to flee away on 15-05-2000. 

 8. The prosecution examined as many as 13 witnesses in support of its his case but the defence examined none. 

 23. PW 18 Md. Inamul Haque, S.I. who is an Investigation Officer. He visited the place of occurrence and prepared the sketch map and index. He obtained the statements under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and he also recorded 164 statements of the Code of Criminal Procedure from the accused and the victim and he tried to arrest the absconded accused. After conclusion of the investigation having found a prima facie case submitted the charge-sheet being No. 85 dated 25-7-2000 under sections 5,6 and 30 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000. In the cross-examination he stated that the convict Nazrul's house is situated one and half miles away from Indian Border. He also examined the transport employees of Druti Paribahan who carried some of the victim from Dhaka and asked the supervisors of total 3(three) transport authorities. He also stated that the accused Saiful and others collected the victims in order to traffic them to India and he also recorded the statement of local people. 

 26. Mr. A. Y. Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the Mohor Ali and Nazrul Islam in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 33624 of 2010 and 9833 of 2008 submits that there are inconsistent and discrepancies in the statements made by the prosecution witnesses, in particular, as to the place of occurrence being Gobindopur and Ratnashar which are situated in different arrears, therefore, the prosecution has shifted from F.I.R. story as such, the Rule should be made absolute. The learned Advocate further submits that the requirements of sections 87 and 88 of the Code of Criminal Procedure have not been complied with for absconded convicts therefore, the trial and the judgment thereof are liable to be set-aside. 

 27. Mr. Sarwar Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant Md. Ismail in Criminal Appeal No. 1773 of 2002 submits that the appellant was not caught red handed at the time of the alleged recovery of the women who were about to traffic to India. but he was named by the other co- convicts, as such , the conviction is liable to be set-aside as being passed out of conjecture and surmise, therefore, the appeal should be allowed and the aforesaid impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence should be set-aside. The learned Advocate further submits that the appellant was in hospital on the date of occurrence, as such, it is not believable story that he was involved at all with the offence as alleged. He further submits that there were as many as 30 witnesses but the vital witnesses who recovered the victims being the local people, like, Jabbar and Shawkat were not examined, therefore, the prosecution witnesses are not sufficient to convict the appellant. He also submits that out of 7 victims who are P.Ws, only Parveen, PW 4, disclosed his name but there are no sufficient evidence thereabout. Finally the learned Advocate submits that examination of a convict under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the learned Judge was under an obligation to put all incriminating statements, circumstances and evidences made by the PWs to him and failure to comply such provision makes the prosecution case fatal and the conviction should be set-aside on that ground. 

 28. The Rules and the appeals were opposed by the learned Assistant Attorney-General on behalf of the state. Mr. Bashir Ahmed, submits that the prosecution examined as many as 19 witnesses including the victims who were collected for trafficking to India in order to get the illegal money and the prosecution has proved the guilt of the convict -petitioners/appellants and absconded convicts beyond all reasonable doubt as each and every prosecution witness has corroborated each other In order to prove the prosecution case. He further submits that the learned Judge of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Tribunal, Satkhira after examining the statements of the witnesses and the relevant papers and also the cross-examination on behalf of the defence found the convicts guilty as charged. 

 29. Regarding the submissions on behalf of the petitioners in Criminal Miscellaneous Cases and regarding the procedure laid down under section 87 and 88 of the Code of Criminal Procedure he submits that Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 is a special law containing self sufficient procedural matters for the trial for an offender who committed the offence under this law. In this regard, he referred to section 21 of the Nari-o-Shishu Ain, 2000 which provides a procedure to try an accused in absentia and in the instant case this procedure have been complied with. 

 32. Regarding the submissions made by the learned advocate Mr. AY Ahmed Ali appearing for the petitioners in Criminal Miscellaneous Cases about the sections 87 and 88 of the Code of Criminal Procedure we considered that an offence alleged against the convicts are under a special law being Nari-o-Shishu Ain which contained section 21 for trial of accused in absentia. Section 21 of the Ain is also reproduced below:— 

 33. From the above, we consider that for an offence under a special law, its trial and its all procedures should be continuing and concluded under the provisions of the special law. Following the requirements of section 21 of the Ain, 2000 is sufficient for trial in absentia. In the instant case, from the LC Records it appears that the prosecution has sufficiently and clearly followed the provision as required by this special law for the trial of the absconded convicts. Regarding the submissions made by the learned Advocate Mr. Sarwar Ahmed for appellant Ismail as to his submission under the procedure to be followed under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. We have carefully examined section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which is reproduced below:— 

 "342. Power to examine the accused-(1) For the purpose of enabling the accused to explain any circumstances appearing in the evidence against him, the Court, may, at any stage of any inquiry or trial without previously warning the accused put such questions to him as the Court considers necessary and shall, for the purpose aforesaid, question him generally on the case after the witnesses for the prosecution have been examined and before he is called on for his defence." 

 34. In the instant case as it appears from the examination under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the learned Judge of the Tribunal has examined and put common question to all the arrested accused in the following manner:— 

 35. In the above circumstances, we consider that there is no procedural defect in examining the convicts at the stage of examination under section 342 of the Code of Criminal procedure and therefore no question of sending back the appeals or miscellaneous cases for retrial from initial stage. After plain reading of section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure it appears that the first part of this section is not mandatory but discretionary so far it relates to putting any question to an accused as to the circumstances appeared in the evidence against him but the second part of this section is mandatory not discretionary as to questioning an accused generally on the case after prosecution witness and before any defence witness. In the instant case, the learned Tribunal put the prosecution case to the convicts and questioned him generally for their reply thereof. In the above circumstances, we find that the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Satkhira committed no error of law in passing the impugned judgment as the prosecution has proved the guilt of the petitioners/appellants beyond all reasonable doubt. In addition, we hope that the state shall take all precautionary measure to protect vulnerable women and children who become easy prey of the culprits sometime at the cost of their life. 

 36. In the result, the Rules in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 33624 of 2010 and 9833 of 2008 are hereby discharged and the Criminal Appeal No. 1773 of 2002 and the Jail Appeal No. 387 of 2002 are hereby dismissed. 

 37. Accordingly, the judgment and order dated 20-05-2002 passed in Nari-o-Shishu Case No. 177 of 2000 arising out of Kaligonj Police Station Case No. 09 dated 16-5-2000 corresponding to GR No. 189 of 2000 by the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Satkhira convicting the petitioners/appellants under sections 5, 6 and 30 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Ain, 2000 and sentencing them to suffer imprisonment for life and also to pay a fine of Tk. 5,000 each in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year more is hereby affirmed. 

 38. The petitioners in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 33624 of 2010 and 9833 of 2008 and the appellant in Criminal Appeal No. 1773 of 2002 are hereby directed to surrender before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Satkhira to serve out their remaining portion of the sentence.
